page: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server configured with eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs from the Hopper architecture, providing a total of 637 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8481C processors, delivering 208 vCPUs across 104 physical cores at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. This configuration includes 1872 GB of system memory, yielding 9.0 GB of RAM per core. Notably, this server does not include local SSD storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with the Passmark CPU score and stress-ng multi-core tests ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is also highly optimized, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 423.79 GB/sec and cached small-block reads at 13241.56 GB/sec. The system demonstrates strong capabilities in specialized workloads, achieving top-tier results in Geekbench ray tracing, image processing, and Redis SET operations. For language model workloads, the server processes 7B model prompts at 5430.06 tokens/sec and generates text at 189.54 tokens/sec, placing it in the top 10% for LLM inference.

While multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are exceptional, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Passmark memory scores falling into the average category. The absence of local SSD storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, meaning high-throughput local disk operations are not natively supported without network-attached storage. Given the high density of H100 GPUs and massive system memory, this server is highly cost-efficient for large-scale parallel processing tasks rather than single-threaded applications. It is best suited for deep learning training, large language model inference, advanced data science, and highly parallel compute-intensive simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server designed for highly parallel, compute-intensive workloads. It features eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs with 637 GB of total VRAM, paired with 208 vCPUs from dedicated Intel Xeon 8481C processors running at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 1872 GB of RAM, though it lacks local SSD storage, requiring external storage configurations. Benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and superior LLM inference capabilities, particularly for prompt processing and text generation on medium-sized models. Conversely, single-core performance and memory scores remain average. This high-density hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for massive parallel processing but represents a tradeoff for single-threaded tasks or workloads requiring local high-speed disk storage. It is highly suited for large-scale AI training, LLM inference, and complex data science pipelines.
